1.1: These the words of Amos—a regular dude from Tekoa who used to watch sheep—He saw this vision from the Lord 'bout Israel, back when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam (son of Joash) was king of Israel—two years before that big earthquake shook everything.
1.2: He said: "The Lord roarin' from Zion, His voice thunderin' outta Jerusalem. Shepherd fields turnin' sad, and Mount Carmel? Witherin' dry."
1.3: This what the Lord say: "I done let Damascus slide three times… but that fourth one? Nah, it's a wrap. They went too far when they crushed Gilead like grain—used iron tools, no mercy.
1.4: So I'ma send fire to Hazael's house. It's gon' burn down Ben-Hadad's palaces.
1.5: I'ma break down the gate in Damascus, wipe out the folks chillin' in the Valley of Aven, and knock down the ruler in Beth Eden. Syria's people? They goin' into exile in Kir," says the Lord.
1.6: The Lord said: "Gaza done messed up three times—and the fourth time was it. They took a whole group of captives and sold 'em off to Edom.
1.7: So I'ma light Gaza's wall up in flames. The fire gon' eat up all their fancy buildings.
1.8: I'ma silence Ashdod's people, shut down the king in Ashkelon. My hand gon' hit Ekron too. And the rest of the Philistines? Gone," says the Lord God.
1.9: The Lord said: "Tyre got three strikes… and then one more. They sold folks out to Edom too, broke a sacred bond, forgot that brotherhood ain't just a word.
1.10: So I'ma send fire on Tyre's walls. Them palaces? Gone in the blaze."
1.11: The Lord said: "Edom? You on the list too. You chased your brother with a sword, showed no mercy, held onto your hate like it was a trophy, kept that grudge burning forever.
1.12: So I'ma drop fire on Teman, and it's gon' eat up Bozrah too."
1.13: The Lord said: "Ammon? You wild for this. Three strikes plus one. Y'all ripped open pregnant women in Gilead—just to stretch your borders.
1.14: So I'ma burn down the walls of Rabbah, and that fire gon' hit hard—right in the middle of war cries, with a storm like a whirlwind tearing through.
1.15: Their king and all his royal boys? They all goin' into captivity," says the Lord.

2.1: This what the Lord say: "Moab? You crossed a line too. Three strikes, then four. You burned the bones of Edom's king, grinded 'em down like he was nothin' but dust.
2.2: So I'ma set Moab on fire. Kerioth's palaces? Gone. Moab gon' fall with screams and trumpet blasts.
2.3: I'ma wipe out their judges, and all them princes? They fall with 'em," says the Lord.
2.4: The Lord said: "Judah… yeah, I got y'all number too. Three sins, four sins—I ain't holdin' back no more. Y'all disrespected My law, straight-up ignored My commandments. Y'all followin' lies that been passed down like they tradition.
2.5: So I'ma send fire on Judah, and it's gon' burn through Jerusalem's palaces."
2.6: This what the Lord say: "Israel—yeah, y'all too. Three strikes wasn't enough—y'all did four and more. You sell out righteous folk for money. Sell out the poor for a pair of sandals like they cheap.
2.7: Y'all trample the dust on the heads of the poor, twistin' justice outta shape. Then you got men and they daddies sleepin' with the same woman—defilin' My name like it don't mean nothin'.
2.8: Y'all lay down at altars on clothes you took from folks who owe you, then drink wine you got off unjust fines—in My house at that!
2.9: "Y'all forgot who cleared the path for you? I'm the One who took down the Amorites—they was tall like cedar trees and strong like oaks. But I chopped down they fruit and dug up they roots.
2.10: I brought y'all up outta Egypt. Led you forty years through that wilderness, gave you the Amorites' land like it was yours.
2.11: I even raised up your sons to be prophets. Had some of y'all young men dedicated as Nazirites. Ain't that true, Israel?" says the Lord.
2.12: "Instead of honoring that, y'all gave them Nazirites wine, and told My prophets: 'Shut up. Don't speak.'
2.13: So now? I'm feelin' the weight of y'all mess like a wagon overloaded with grain.
2.14: The fast ones? They ain't gettin' away. The strong? They won't find no power. The mighty? Can't even save themselves.
2.15: Archers gon' drop they bows. The quick ones ain't fast enough. Even the horse riders can't escape.
2.16: The bravest warriors? They gon' run away butt-naked when the day hits," says the Lord.

3.1: Listen up to what the Lord sayin', Israel—yeah, I'm talkin' to the whole fam I brought outta Egypt.
3.2: Y'all the only ones I picked outta all the families on earth. That's exactly why I gotta check y'all for y'all sins.
3.3: Two folks can't walk together unless they on the same page, right?
3.4: A lion don't roar in the woods if he ain't caught nothin'. A young lion ain't gon' growl in his den if he empty.
3.5: A bird don't fall in a trap unless a trap's been set. And traps don't snap shut for no reason.
3.6: If a warning horn blows in the city, folks gon' panic, right? If disaster hits a city, don't you think God had His hand in it?
3.7: Look—God don't do nothin' unless He tell His prophets what's comin' first.
3.8: The lion already roared—how you not scared? The Lord done spoke—how can I not speak what He told me?
3.9: Go ahead—announce this in the big houses of Ashdod and Egypt. Tell 'em to pull up and watch what's goin' down on the hills of Samaria. It's chaos in the streets. People gettin' done dirty on every corner.
3.10: These folks don't even know how to do right no more, says the Lord. All they know is how to stash up violence and stolen goods in their cribs.
3.11: So this what God say: "An enemy gon' surround your land. They gon' drain you of your strength, and they gon' rob your mansions clean."
3.12: And the Lord says this too: "Just like a shepherd tryin' to snatch a couple legs or an ear outta a lion's mouth, that's how little gon' be left of y'all in Samaria—just them chillin' on the edge of the bed or couch."
3.13: Hear this and speak out against Jacob's house, says the Lord God, the Commander of everything:
3.14: "On the day I check Israel for all they mess, I'ma also shut down Bethel's altars. The horns on them altars? Snapped off and hittin' the dirt."
3.15: "I'ma destroy them winter homes and summer homes, all them ivory cribs gon' be gone, and them big ol' fancy houses? That's the end of all that," says the Lord.

4.1: Listen here, you bougie women of Bashan, livin' high up in Samaria—the ones who oppress the poor, crush the ones in need, and stay tellin' your men, "Bring me somethin' to sip on!"
4.2: The Lord God swore on His holiness: "Look, the days comin' where y'all gon' be dragged away with fishhooks—you and your kids too.
4.3: Y'all gon' be pushed out through busted-up walls, each one marchin' straight out, and thrown into Harmon," says the Lord.
4.4: "Go ahead, keep showin' up to Bethel—just to sin more. Hit Gilgal too—keep stackin' up them transgressions. Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days like you somebody.
4.5: Make a big show outta your 'thanksgiving offerings'—with yeast in it. Announce your little 'freewill gifts' real loud—'cause y'all love performin'," says the Lord God.
4.6: "I made sure y'all felt hunger—empty mouths, no bread in sight. Still… y'all didn't come back to Me," says the Lord.
4.7: "I stopped the rain three months before harvest. Some cities got showers, others got nothin'. Whole towns had to travel just to find water—but even then? Still didn't return to Me," says the Lord.
4.8: "So two or three cities had to go wanderin' to another town just to find water—but even then, they ain't get enough to satisfy 'em. Still, y'all didn't come back to Me," says the Lord.
4.9: "I hit your gardens with blight. Mildew ate up the vineyards, the figs, the olives. Locusts snatched up the rest—still, y'all ain't come back," says the Lord.
4.10: "I hit y'all with plagues like I did Egypt. Your young men got taken out in battle, horses too—your camps stank to high heaven—and still… y'all ain't come back," says the Lord.
4.11: "I shook some of y'all like Sodom and Gomorrah—left you barely makin' it out like a log pulled from a fire. Still… y'all ain't come back to Me," says the Lord.
4.12: "So here's what's next, Israel—since I gotta do all this to get your attention… prepare to meet your God, Israel!"
4.13: 'Cause look—He's the one who shaped the mountains, breathed wind into the world, reads thoughts before you even say 'em, turns the sunrise into dark, and steps high on the earth like He own it. That's the Lord God of Heaven's Armies. That's His name.

5.1: Listen to this word I'm speakin' against y'all—yeah, it's a whole funeral cry, House of Israel:
5.2: "The daughter of Israel done fell flat. She ain't gettin' back up. She laid out in her land, and ain't nobody comin' to help her rise."
5.3: The Lord God says: "A city that used to send out a thousand? Only a hundred gon' come back. And a city that sent out a hundred? Only ten gon' survive."
5.4: This what the Lord say to Israel: "Come find Me—and live.
5.5: But don't go runnin' to Bethel. Don't try to slide through Gilgal. Don't even think about passin' through Beersheba. Gilgal gettin' locked up. Bethel? It's finished."
5.6: "Seek the Lord and live—before He shows up like a wildfire on Joseph's house and burns it to the ground—and ain't nobody in Bethel able to put it out."
5.7: Y'all the type to flip justice into bitterness, and toss righteousness out like trash.
5.8: He the One who made the stars—Pleiades and Orion. Turns death-dark nights into bright mornin's, and flips the day dark like it's midnight. He pulls ocean water up and pours it out all over the earth. The Lord is His name.
5.9: He rains destruction on the powerful, tearin' down strongholds like they made of paper.
5.10: Y'all can't stand folks who tell the truth in public. Anybody who speaks up straight? You hate them.
5.11: That's why, since you trample the poor and hit 'em with grain taxes—even though y'all livin' in fancy cut-stone houses, you won't be livin' in 'em long. You planted vineyards, but you won't get a single sip.
5.12: I see all y'all dirt. Yeah, all of it: You mistreat good people, take bribes like it's normal, and block justice from the folks who need it most.
5.13: That's why the wise ones keep quiet—'cause this whole time is wicked and heavy.
5.14: Chase good, not evil—so you can live. Then maybe the Lord God of Heaven's Armies will actually be with y'all like you say He is.
5.15: Hate what's evil. Love what's good. Let justice show up at the city gates. Maybe then God'll show mercy to what's left of Joseph's people.
5.16: The Lord God of Hosts says this: It's gon' be cryin' in every street, folks yellin' "Oh no! Oh no!" in every hood. They gon' call in farmers to mourn, and professional wailers to do what they do.
5.17: Even in the vineyards where folks usually celebrate? Tears everywhere. 'Cause I'm passin' through, says the Lord.
5.18: Y'all talkin' like y'all want the Day of the Lord. But why? What good is it gon' do you? It's gon' be all darkness, not light.
5.19: Like somebody runnin' from a lion—only to get jumped by a bear. Or thinkin' they safe at home, leanin' on the wall—and then a snake bites 'em.
5.20: Yeah, the Day of the Lord ain't light—it's deep dark. Ain't a glimmer of brightness in it.
5.21: "I hate your feast days. I can't stand your religious meetups.
5.22: All them burnt offerings and grain gifts? I ain't touchin' 'em. Your peace offerings? Nah."
5.23: "Turn off that noise you call worship music. I don't wanna hear your instruments singin'.
5.24: What I do wanna hear? Justice rollin' like a river. Righteousness flowin' like a strong stream."
5.25: "Y'all really think y'all brought Me sacrifices back in the wilderness for forty years, Israel? Nah.
5.26: Y'all was carryin' Sikkuth—y'all own little king idol. Holdin' up Chiun, your handmade stars and gods. Idols y'all put together your own selves."
5.27: "That's why I'ma send y'all into exile—way past Damascus," says the Lord—the One they call the God of Heaven's Armies.

6.1: Woe to y'all sittin' pretty in Zion, actin' safe in Samaria. You high-ranking folks in the top nation, the ones everybody runnin' to for answers.
6.2: Go look at Calneh. Slide through Hamath. Take a trip down to Gath in Philistia. Y'all think y'all better than them? Y'all think your land go further than theirs?
6.3: Woe to the ones pushin' judgment day far off, but bringin' violence closer with every move.
6.4: Y'all loungin' on ivory beds, stretchin' out on couches like y'all royalty. Feastin' on lamb chops and stall-fed veal like it's a cookout every day.
6.5: Strummin' on harps with nothin' but vibes, makin' new instruments like David—but no depth.
6.6: Sippin' wine outta bowls (not cups), oilin' up with the finest scents—but y'all don't shed one tear for what Joseph's people goin' through.
6.7: That's why y'all gon' be the first ones taken when the judgment hits. All y'all reclinin' at banquets? Y'all up next to go.
6.8: The Lord God swore on His own name—the Commander of Heaven's Armies said: "I can't stand the pride of Jacob. I hate these palaces y'all livin' in. That whole city? It's gettin' handed over. Everything in it."
6.9: When it goes down, even if ten folks hide out in one house—they all gon' die.
6.10: And when a relative comes through with the person assigned to cremate, and they carryin' out the bodies, they gon' ask the last person inside, "Anybody left?" And that person gon' whisper, "Nah." And they'll say, "Shhh! Don't even mention God's name right now."
6.11: The Lord commandin' it: The big houses? Smashed to bits. The small ones? Splintered too.
6.12: Do horses run on cliffs? Do folks plow rocks with oxen? Nope. But y'all flipped justice into poison, and righteousness into something bitter.
6.13: Y'all boastin' about Lo Debar like it's a big win. Y'all braggin', "Didn't we snatch Karnaim by our own strength?"
6.14: "I'ma raise up a whole nation against y'all," says the Lord, Commander of Heaven's Armies. "And they gon' press y'all hard—from the entrance of Hamath all the way to the valley of Arabah."

7.1: The Lord God gave me a vision: I saw Him callin' up a swarm of locusts right after the king took his cut of the crops—so this was the last harvest for regular folks.
7.2: When the locusts finished eatin' everything green, I cried out: "Lord God, please forgive! Jacob (Israel) can't take this—he too small!"
7.3: And the Lord changed His mind. "Aight. This one ain't gon' happen," said the Lord.
7.4: Then the Lord gave me another vision: He called for judgment by fire. That fire went deep—burned all the underground water and scorched the land.
7.5: So I cried again: "Lord God, please stop! Jacob too small—he can't survive this!"
7.6: And the Lord changed His mind again. "This one too—ain't gon' happen," said the Lord.
7.7: Then I saw the Lord standin' on a straight wall, holdin' a plumb line in His hand.
7.8: He asked me, "Amos, what you see?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said: "I'm settin' this plumb line right in the middle of My people, Israel. I ain't gon' overlook they mess no more.
7.9: Them high places of Isaac? Gon' be abandoned. Them temples in Israel? Wrecked. And I'ma bring the sword against Jeroboam's house."
7.10: Then Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, ran to King Jeroboam talkin' slick: "Yo, Amos out here stirrin' up rebellion in the kingdom. People can't handle what he preachin'—it's too much."
7.11: "He sayin' Jeroboam gon' die by the sword and Israel gon' be dragged out their own land."
7.12: Amaziah pulled up on Amos like: "Look here, prophet-man—go back to Judah where you from. Make your money and preach over there.
7.13: But don't come back prophesyin' at Bethel. This here's the king's sanctuary—royal property."
7.14: Amos clapped back: "Man, I wasn't even a prophet. Ain't come from no line of prophets. I was out here takin' care of sheep and sycamore trees.
7.15: But the Lord found me while I was mindin' my business in the field, and He told me, 'Go speak to My people, Israel.'"
7.16: "So listen up— You told me to stop prophesyin' and not to speak against Israel? Cool. But here's what God got to say:"
7.17: "Your wife gon' end up sellin' herself in the streets. Your sons and daughters? Killed by the sword. Your land? Divided and sold off. You? Gon' die in some unclean foreign place. And Israel? Yeah, they definitely gettin' snatched out they land."

8.1: The Lord God gave me another vision: I saw a basket full of summer fruit.
8.2: God said, "Amos, what you see?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the Lord said: "Exactly. Just like that fruit is ripe, so is Israel. Their time is up. I ain't gon' overlook they mess no more."
8.3: "In that day, the songs in the temple? Gon' be funeral cries. Bodies everywhere—folk gettin' tossed out in silence like trash," says the Lord God.
8.4: "Listen up, y'all who crush the needy and keep the poor from ever gettin' ahead—
8.5: Y'all be sayin', 'Man, when the New Moon festival over so we can get back to sellin'? When Sabbath done so we can get back to grindin'? Let's rig the weights, shrink the product, raise the prices...
8.6: sell folks into debt slavery for a few coins, and even push spoiled wheat just to keep profitin'?'"
8.7: The Lord swore on the pride of Jacob: "I promise, I ain't gon' forget a single thing y'all done."
8.8: "Don't you think the land should quake for this? Ain't everybody in it gon' mourn? It'll rise and fall like the Nile—swelling, flooding, then pulling back."
8.9: "On that day," says the Lord God, "I'll make the sun set at noon. Middle of the day, whole sky go black.
8.10: Y'all parties gon' turn into funerals, songs into cries, sackcloth on your waist, shaved heads in grief. Y'all gon' mourn like you just lost your only child. And by the end? It's gon' be a day y'all never forget—and not in a good way."
8.11: "Days comin'," says the Lord, "when I'll send a famine to the land. Not a hunger for food. Not a thirst for water. But folks gon' be starvin' to hear a word from Me.
8.12: They gon' roam coast to coast, run from north to east, lookin' high and low for the Word of the Lord—but they ain't gon' find it."
8.13: "In that day, even the pretty young girls and strong young men gon' pass out from spiritual thirst.
8.14: The ones who swear by them false gods in Samaria, who say, 'As your god lives, O Dan!' or, 'Long live the way of Beersheba!' Yeah—they all gon' fall and not get back up."

9.1: I saw the Lord standin' by the altar, and He said: "Hit them pillars so hard the whole foundation shakes. Let the roof fall in on their heads. And the ones that make it out? I'ma finish them with the sword. Ain't nobody runnin'. Ain't nobody hidin'. Ain't nobody safe."
9.2: "If they dig way down in hell? I'ma snatch 'em up. If they climb all the way up to heaven? I'ma bring 'em down.
9.3: Hide on top of Mount Carmel? I'm comin' for 'em. Dive to the bottom of the ocean? I'ma send a sea monster to bite 'em.
9.4: Try to blend in with the captives? The sword still gon' find 'em. I'm watchin' 'em—not for good, but for judgment."
9.5: The Lord God of Heaven's Armies— He just touch the earth and it melts. Folks mourn everywhere. The land rise and fall like the Nile.
9.6: He got skyscraper layers in the sky, and He laid the earth's foundation deep. He calls water out the sea and floods the land with it. The Lord is His name.
9.7: "Y'all think y'all special, Israel? Ain't y'all the same as the Ethiopians to Me?" says the Lord. "I brought y'all outta Egypt, yeah... But didn't I also bring the Philistines outta Caphtor? And the Syrians outta Kir?"
9.8: "I see that sinful kingdom. And I'ma wipe it off the face of the earth. But I ain't gon' completely destroy the whole house of Jacob," says the Lord.
9.9: "I'ma sift Israel through the nations like a farmer sifts grain. And not one lil' kernel of the faithful gon' be lost.
9.10: But the sinners—the arrogant ones talkin' 'ain't nothin' bad gon' happen to us'? They gon' die by the sword."
9.11: "But in that day, I'ma rebuild David's house that fell apart. I'ma fix what's broke, raise up what's ruined, and bring it back like the good old days.
9.12: And My people gon' take over what's left of Edom and all the nations that bear My name," says the Lord who's really doin' all this.
9.13: "Listen—days comin' where the plowman gon' catch up with the reaper, and the grape stomper gon' run into the seed sower. Mountains gon' be drippin' wine, and hills gon' flow with it."
9.14: "I'ma bring My people back. They gon' rebuild the ruined cities and move in. They gon' plant vineyards and drink from 'em. Grow gardens and eat they own fruit."
9.15: "And when I plant 'em this time? They ain't gettin' pulled up again. They gon' stay in the land I gave 'em," says the Lord your God.
